title: 01_industry_risk_matrix
text: Industry Risk Matrix Version: 1.0 | Last updated: 2025-09-18 Purpose This document defines the industry risk categories used during credit risk assessments. Industry Risk Ratings Low Risk Industries - Utilities - Government - Healthcare Medium Risk Industries - Manufacturing - FMCG Distribution - IT Services High Risk Industries - Construction - Real Estate Developers - Airlines - Commodity Trading - Startups - Mining & Metal Assessment Guidance Industry risk is one factor within the overall credit assessment process. Lower-risk industries typically demonstrate more stable demand, predictable cash flows, and lower business volatility. Higher-risk industries may experience cyclical demand, market volatility, project-based revenue fluctuations, funding challenges, or regulatory uncertainty. Review industry classification carefully before assigning a risk rating.

title: 02_credit_risk_assessment_process
text: Credit Risk Assessment Process Version: 1.0 | Last updated: 2025-10-02 Objective Assess customer creditworthiness using document verification, compliance validation, financial analysis, external bureau data, and industry risk evaluation. Process Overview Step 1 Verify Company Registration Certificate and GST Certificate are available. Step 2 Confirm the client company name matches both submitted certificates. Step 3 Verify company legal status through the MCA database. Step 4 Review sanctions, watchlists, and compliance findings from approved compliance screening sources. Step 5 Collect financial statements for the previous two financial years. Step 6 Calculate key financial ratios from the latest financial year: - Current Ratio - Debt-to-Equity Ratio - Net Profit Margin Step 7 Retrieve the latest external credit bureau score. Step 8 Assign an Industry Risk Rating using the Industry Risk Matrix. Step 9 Determine the final risk outcome and recommended credit terms. Day 3 Focus Day 3 retrieval exercises focus only on Step 8 Industry Risk Rating. Other assessment steps are included for business context only.
